 Canadiens @ Blues: Game preview, start time, Tale of the Tape, and how to watch
 The third game of the road trip has the Canadiens in St. Louis looking for their first three-game winning streak.
 Posted on October 27, 2026 October 27, 2026 by Justin Blades 
 Photo by Keith Gillett/Icon Sportswire 
 How to watch
 Game 12: Montreal Canadiens @ St. Louis Blues
 Start time:  **8:00 PM EDT / 5:00 PM PDT** 
In the Canadiens region: TSN2 (English), RDS (French)
In the Blues region: STLNHL 
Streaming: TSN+, RDS (Canada), ESPN+ (USA)
 Two games into a road trip the Montreal Canadiens learned they’d be embarking upon without their captain, they have already guaranteed themselves at least a .500 performance. A sound effort in Chicago was followed up with a relatively steady one in Winnipeg for the Heritage Classic, where Jacob Fowler made up for all but one of the minor defensive mistakes in the final half of the game. The Canadiens did well to get out to a multi-goal lead for the seventh time in 11 games, and held on for the two points.
 The trip has taken the Canadiens south to St. Louis where they’re looking for a third consecutive victory. The Blues were one of just two teams Montreal didn’t take a point from in 2025-26 (along with the San Jose Sharks), and issues that have affected the team this year were the responsible for the two regulation losses. In the opening match, a one-goal lead turned into a one-goal deficit through just 65 seconds of the second period, and the Canadiens were unable to recover. The power play failed them in the second game, unable to convert on four power-plays including a long five-on-three, and stood as one of the four shutout performance they were dealt in an otherwise great offensive season.

 St. Louis was only shut out on two occasions in 2025-26, but they scored two goals or fewer on 36 occasions, ranking 24th in goals with just 230. That output wasn’t nearly enough to contend in the Central Division, and the off-season was spent attempting to address it.
 After a season of rumours and a disappointing 46 points after four years contributing around 70, Jordan Kyrou was traded to the Washington Capitals, netting Connor McMichael along with a first-round pick. St. Louis was also the team that landed Mason McTavish, another player long rumoured to be on the trading block, with that outcome in Anaheim only made more likely when McTavish was a healthy scratch for a couple of games in the post-season.
 So far both trades are working out well. McMichael has seven points in 11 games, while McTavish shares the team lead with Jimmy Snuggerud for goals with six, and is even with Dylan Holloway on 10 points. That offence has been important as Robert Thomas, annually the team’s top scorer, has gotten off to a slow start without Kyrou on his wing, with just six points. The newcomers have helped the Blues begin the season with a 5-5-1 record, not good enough to hold a playoff position, but at least holding them in the race early.
